findings.issue: Governance gate design defect (pre-existing, not introduced by T-0763). FF-5's router.ts guard has two branches: (a) `git diff --quiet origin/dev -- src/http/router.ts` — a real merge-base-relative check that correctly fires on this task's genuine additive diff (verified: exit 1 on this branch, i.e. it DOES detect the divergence); (b) but instead of failing there, the script falls through to `git diff --quiet HEAD -- src/http/router.ts` — working-tree-vs-own-HEAD, which is vacuously empty for ANY committed state, additive or destructive. Empirically reproduced live: with an uncommitted one-line append to router.ts, FF-5 correctly FAILs ('has been modified'); reverting the edit and re-running on the clean committed tree, FF-5 PASSes via the fallback ('unchanged in this branch') even though `git diff origin/dev -- router.ts` still shows a real, substantial diff at that same moment. FF-5 therefore does not protect router.ts against committed modifications at all (additive or otherwise) — it only catches mid-edit/uncommitted state. It happens to be harmless here because the actually-authoritative gate for router.ts additivity is FF-HIRE-4 (agent-hire-frozen-additive.sh), which IS merge-base-correct and DOES gate deleted-line-count against the true merge-base — independently re-run and confirmed PASS (0 deleted lines) in this review. Filing as a non-blocking follow-up candidate: 'FF-5's router.ts branch should also diff against merge-base (or drop the working-tree-vs-HEAD fallback entirely, since FF-HIRE-4 already covers the additive-only invariant for this file).
findings.suggestion: Follow-up task: change worker-auth-public-surface.sh's router.ts check to diff against merge-base with dev (mirroring FF-HIRE-4's BASE= resolution) instead of falling back to HEAD, or remove the fallback branch and let FF-HIRE-4 be the sole authority for router.ts additivity.
